methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series C → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.7x) to $400M last post money.

data.narrative:
AiDash is a Series C-stage infrastructure and logistics software company founded by Abhishek Singh. The company has raised $91M+ to date. Valuation analysis is constrained by an absence of direct public comparables and insufficient disclosed private peer transactions in the infrastructure software space to support a robust multiples-based approach.

The single applicable valuation method employed is stage-progression analysis, which anchors to AiDash's last known post-money valuation of $400M and applies a 1.7x step-up multiplier typical of Series C to subsequent-stage advancement. This methodology yields an implied valuation of $680M. The 1.7x step-up reflects standard dilution and risk-adjusted return expectations for growth-stage infrastructure software, absent company-specific performance data or revised investor terms.

The triangulated valuation range spans $578M (low) to $782M (high), with $680M as the median point. This narrow band reflects reliance on a single method; the range widens modestly to capture typical variance in stage-progression assumptions. Key uncertainties include the absence of comparable company multiples to validate the step-up assumption, lack of disclosed financial metrics (ARR, gross margin, burn rate, customer concentration) to benchmark against sector norms, and unknown changes in capital market conditions or company trajectory since the $400M valuation. Resolution of these uncertainties through disclosure or additional transaction data would substantively improve valuation confidence.
